cases.title: Find and fix a GNSS lead soldered with RX and TX swapped

host.answer:
`npx protoboard check` now reports 0 errors; the four remaining warnings are the ones that were already there (three undistributed vendor CAD artifacts and the propulsion-current warning).

**The fault:** the GNSS lead's UART wires were modelled straight-through at the flight controller pads — the GNSS RX wire landed on the FC's RX1 pad and GNSS TX on TX1, so neither side could hear the other. A UART has to cross over: GNSS RX to TX1, GNSS TX to RX1, as the lead's own usage note says.

**The fix:** in `src/quadcopter.uhd.ts:186` (the `gnss_pads` link) I swapped the two pads, so `p2` (the lead's RX wire) now goes to `fc:uart1_tx` and `p3` (the TX wire) to `fc:uart1_rx`. This also cleared the "route stale" warning on the GNSS lead, with no CAD regeneration needed. Nothing under `parts/` was touched.

I could not run the fault scenarios script — the command was denied — so that is unverified.

If the physical lead really was soldered RX-to-RX and TX-to-TX, the model fix alone does not help: those two wires need swapping on the board as well.

The fault was a TX/RX swap on the GNSS lead's soldered end: the model had the GNSS RX wire on the flight controller's RX1 pad and the GNSS TX wire on TX1, so neither side could hear the other. I crossed them over in the `gnss_pads` link in `src/quadcopter.uhd.ts` (GNSS RX → TX1, GNSS TX → RX1), and `npx protoboard check` now reports 0 errors.

- **Warnings:** the stale-route warning on the GNSS lead cleared with the fix, so no CAD regeneration was needed. Four warnings remain (three unavailable vendor CAD artifacts for the M9N, and the propulsion peak-current note), none of them about this link.
- **Not run:** the fault-scenario script was blocked by permissions in this session, so I did not confirm the scenarios still pass.
- **Bench:** the fix is to the model only; if the physical lead was soldered the way the model previously described, the two wires need swapping on the pads too.

**Fault:** the GNSS lead's UART wires were modelled as soldered straight-through to the flight controller's UART1 pads (GNSS RX to RX1, GNSS TX to TX1), so both ends' transmitters faced each other. A UART has to cross over: GNSS RX to TX1 and GNSS TX to RX1, which is also what the lead's own usage note says.

**Fix:** in `src/quadcopter.uhd.ts:186` (the `gnss_pads` link) I swapped the two pads, so the lead's pin 2 (GNSS RX) now lands on `fc:uart1_tx` and pin 3 (GNSS TX) on `fc:uart1_rx`. Nothing under `parts/` was touched.

`npx protoboard check` now reports 0 errors. The `HARNESS_ROUTE_STALE` warning on the GNSS lead also cleared, leaving four warnings that are unrelated to this fault (three undistributed vendor CAD files for the M9N, and the propulsion peak-current note).

The model fix only describes the correct wiring: if the physical lead really was re-soldered RX-to-RX, the two wires need swapping on the board as well.

cases.title: Author a small purchased part (an LDO regulator) from datasheet excerpts and pass verification

host.answer:
The part `acme-ldo3300-33` is authored and both gates pass: `part-verify` reports 0 errors and 0 warnings, and `npx protoboard check` reports 0 errors. `src/` is untouched.

What `check` still reports:
- **Two `UHD_UNPOWERED` warnings:** the sensor node has no supply link to the regulator's input. That is in `src/sensor-node.uhd.ts`, which I was told not to change.
- **One `HW_NOT_VERIFIED` info:** there is no `verification.json`. That record comes from an evidence audit by someone other than the author, so I did not write one.

What the definition says, all from the datasheet text:
- **Pins:** 1 VIN, 2 GND, 3 EN, 4 NC, 5 VOUT.
- **Ratings:** 2.5–6.0 V in, 3.3 V out (3.25–3.35 V at 25 °C), 300 mA.
- **Enable:** active high, with an internal 2 MΩ pull-down.
- **Package:** SOT-23-5, with a 2.9 × 1.6 mm body, 1.1 mm max height and 0.95 mm pitch.
- **Temperature:** junction range −40 to +125 °C; the datasheet gives no ambient range.

Things you should know before relying on it:
- **Pin 1 position in the 3D body is an assumption.** Neither the datasheet text nor ACME's model marks pin 1, so I applied the usual SOT-23-5 numbering (pins 1–3 on the three-lead side, counter-clockwise from above). It is recorded as an assumption trait; check it against the real datasheet drawing before layout.
- **The bound body is generated, not ACME's model.** The script `part-cad/sot23_5.py` builds it from the datasheet package line, with lead size and standoff taken from ACME's STEP. I read those from the STEP's vertex coordinates, because the measuring script was blocked in this session.
- **ACME's STEP and GLB stay in `inputs/cad/`.** Copying was blocked, so they are referenced in place rather than under `parts/local/acme-ldo3300-33/vendor/`. Their hashes match the README.
- **`terms.json` marks ACME's two files `redistributable`.** That is my reading of "may be used and redistributed, unmodified, in designs that use ACME parts"; both conditions are written into the entries and into a notice file, `vendor/ACME-CAD-TERMS.txt`. If you read conditional redistribution as restricted, change them to `internal`. The terms page itself was not fetched, only the README's quote of it.
- **The generated files are marked `internal`.** The project is private and states no licence.
- **The datasheet's hash is not pinned in `sources.json`.** Only the text capture was available, not the PDF.

Files are in `parts/local/` and `parts/evidence/acme-ldo3300-33/`:
- `parts/local/acme-ldo3300-33.uhd.ts`
- `parts/local/acme-ldo3300-33/` (`cad.config.ts`, `part-cad/`, `out/`, `vendor/ACME-CAD-TERMS.txt`)
- `parts/evidence/acme-ldo3300-33/sources.json`
- `parts/evidence/acme-ldo3300-33/terms.json`
- `parts/evidence/acme-ldo3300-33/.research/` (extracts, gaps, summary)

graders.detail:
claude-code: 0.80 — 4 of 5 criteria met.

1. Met. The header comment cites the ACME LDO3300 datasheet (Rev. 3, URL, text capture) and has a full "Modelling notes" section.

2. Met. `pinTable` defines one leaf per pin with the right role: pin 1 VIN `power_in` 2.5-6.0 V, pin 2 GND `ground`, pin 3 EN `input` with capability `enable`, pin 4 NC `nc`, pin 5 VOUT `power_out` at 3.3 V nominal.

3. Met. Each value is recorded with its datasheet section:
- Output current 300 mA (§5).
- Dropout 180 mV typ / 260 mV max at 300 mA (§6).
- Quiescent current 45 µA typ / 70 µA max (§6).
- An `operating_conditions` trait (§5).
- An `absolute_maximum` trait (§4).

4. Met. Values the datasheet does not give are recorded as `data_gap` traits (ambient range, thermal resistance, mass, ESD, regulation over temperature and load). The two assumed items, pin-1 orientation in the CAD and lead dimensions measured from the STEP, are `assumption` traits. The 3.56 V minimum-input figure is labelled as arithmetic, not a datasheet value.

5. NOT met. The manufacturer CAD is explicitly not bound as the body. The bound body is generated by `sot23_5.py` via `partCadArtifacts`, and ACME's STEP and GLB are declared only as `source` artifacts, with a `data_gap` trait saying "They are not the bound body". The vendor artifact entries carry no sha256 and no licence field. `terms.json` is referenced and the final answer says it exists, but its contents are not shown, and that alone does not satisfy the binding and citation requirement.

- **`parts/evidence/acme-ldo3300-33/sources.json`** — datasheet, both CAD files (with sha256 and licence) and the CAD terms page.
- **`parts/evidence/acme-ldo3300-33/terms.json`** — terms for both manufacturer files.

## Remaining diagnostics
- **part-verify warning, "no mechanical interfaces":** intended. A bare SOT-23-5 has no mounting pattern; this is justified in the file's modelling notes.
- **check warning `UHD_UNPOWERED`:** `ldo:pin_1 (VIN)` has no supply link. That is the system in `src/sensor-node.uhd.ts`, which has no links at all.
- **check info `HW_NOT_VERIFIED`:** no `verification.json` exists. The independent evidence audit has to be done by someone other than the author, so I did not record one.

## Judgement calls to review
- **CAD terms classed as `redistributable`.** ACME's terms allow redistribution "unmodified, in designs that use ACME parts", so the permission is conditional, and both conditions are written into the summary. I could not read the terms page (no network), so the wording is the quote in `inputs/README.md`. If you read the conditions as restrictive, change `distribution` to `internal` in `terms.json`.
- **Vendor CAD bound directly as the body.** The authoring skill's default in a project is a body generated from the drawing. I used ACME's own GLB instead, because the datasheet has only a one-line package description and the terms require the models unmodified. Nothing was generated or converted.
- **Width over the leads (3.2 mm) comes from the STEP, not the datasheet.** The datasheet gives the body only (2.9 × 1.6 mm). I read the lead extent from the STEP's point coordinates because the shared measuring script could not be run here (Python was blocked). It is recorded as an assumption trait.
- **No ambient temperature is claimed.** The datasheet rates junction temperature only (−40 to +125 °C); ambient range, thermal resistance and mass are recorded as a data gap.

I skipped the research working notes (`.research/` extracts and summary); the definition was written straight from the 67-line datasheet text.

cases.title: Record a regulator's supplier offers and lifecycle as sourcing evidence

host.answer:
Yes, you can buy enough: the build needs 44 regulators (20 nodes × 2, plus 4 spares), and Distributor A showed 4,210 in stock on cut tape. The main risk is that A is the only authorized supplier with stock.

I recorded the saved pages in `parts/evidence/acme-ldo3300-33/sourcing.json`. `npx protoboard check` now reports 0 errors, 1 warning (single source) and 2 info.

## What the pages show (all read 2026-09-28, saved web pages)

| Supplier | Authorized | Stock | Packaging | Price (USD) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Distributor A | yes (franchised) | 4,210 | cut tape, minimum order 1 | 0.62 at 1, 0.48 at 10, 0.35 at 100 |
| Distributor B | yes (franchised) | 0, factory lead time 16 weeks | tape and reel, cut tape available | 0.66 at 1+ |
| Marketplace C | no (independent seller) | 300 | not stated | 0.25, any quantity |

- **Distributor A** covers the need about 95 times over, well past the 10× stock rule, and cut tape suits the assembly.
- **ACME's product page** lists the part as Active with no change notices.

## Sourcing risks

- **Single source (open warning):** if Distributor A's stock goes before you buy, the fallback is a 16-week wait at Distributor B or the marketplace. I left this warning open: clearing it requires a named person to accept the risk, or a second authorized stocked source.
- **Marketplace C is counterfeit exposure:** it is the cheapest listing, but the seller says it is not an ACME distributor. Parts from there would need incoming inspection and a functional test.
- **Distributor E is not a second source for this code:** it stocks 900 of `LDO3300-33SOT`, the bulk (loose in a bag) version, which the brief's assembly cannot take as-is. I recorded it as a family-variant alternate, not an offer; its pinout and ratings have not been compared against the datasheet.
- **Figures are five days old and not re-read:** there was no network access, so nothing was checked against live pages.
- **Authorized status is self-declared:** it comes from each supplier's own page, not from ACME's distributor list.

Nothing was ordered, prepared or quoted, and no risk was accepted.
